decisions.decision: Phase 1 sub-scope = generalize the existing K8s node monitor (observer + orchestrator + diagnoser/remediator/agent) into a registry-based framework; do NOT implement the other 7 observers/remediators in this phase.
decisions.rationale: User asked 'will it work for k8s pod, ec2, or other services?' — this refactor proves the framework generalizes, and becomes the recipe (ADDING-A-MONITOR.md) for the remaining OBS-*/REM-* work.

decisions.decision: DiagnosisResult.action_type (agent/shared/models.py) changes from a closed Literal to an open str, validated against per-domain THRESHOLDS keys; safety.py FORBIDDEN_OPERATIONS remains the unchanged global floor.
decisions.rationale: Without this, EC2 (reboot_instance) and Postgres (kill_query) action types could never be expressed by Claude — this was identified as the one required change to make the registry pattern actually work for non-k8s domains.

decisions.decision: Extract shared primitives: PreflightResult/_meets_threshold/_log_action/THRESHOLDS -> agent/shared/remediation.py; agent loop -> agent/shared/agent_loop.py::run_tool_loop; diagnoser call -> agent/shared/diagnoser_base.py::diagnose_with_claude; debounce/consumer-group loop -> agent/orchestrators/generic_orchestrator.py; new agent/registry.py with DomainConfig.
decisions.rationale: These are the pieces currently duplicated-by-necessity in node_remediator.py/node_agent.py/node_diagnoser.py/k8s_orchestrator.py that every future domain would otherwise have to copy-paste.

decisions.decision: K8s node monitor behavior (both mode='diagnoser' and mode='agent', including the recent NetworkUnavailable/node_deleted additions) must be unchanged after refactor — this is the acceptance bar.
decisions.rationale: Refactor must be behavior-preserving; node_remediator.py was just verified end-to-end against minikube and that verification should remain valid.
